ki.noCyberbrain: Ki only works from a Cyberbrain. If jamming, every body used in the jamming chain must have a cyberbrain.
ki.biologicalBody: A biological body around the cyberbrain

effect.takeStrain: The Ki infection lashes back through the cyberbrain. Take SV 1d6.

preoccupation.enhance: You become preoccupied with an object you see as unusable or in need of improvement - it does not have to be yours, and the GM decides which one it is. You have to try to improve it with an Extended Hardware Test.
preoccupation.recycle: You become preoccupied with an object you see as unusable or in need of improvement - it does not have to be yours, and the GM decides which one it is. You want to break it down into its components and put those to some other use.
preoccupation.research: You become preoccupied with an object you see as unusable or in need of improvement - it does not have to be yours, and the GM decides which one it is. You want to take it apart far enough to produce a blueprint from it.

reconfiguration.forced: An installed ware system, chosen by the GM, switches itself on and stays continuously active. The cyberbrain can never be chosen.
reconfiguration.shutdown: An installed ware system, chosen by the GM, is completely disabled. The cyberbrain can never be chosen.
reconfiguration.rearranged: The morph rebuilds existing components into a random ware function, chosen by the GM, and disables at least one other ware system in exchange. The cyberbrain can never be chosen.

recalibration.weapon: The infection converts one of your own possessions into a different weapon, chosen by the GM. The replacement is of similar mass and size and serves a similar function. It does not automatically revert to its original form.
recalibration.armor: The infection converts one of your own possessions into a different piece of armor, chosen by the GM. The replacement has roughly the same combined stats (+/- 20%) and serves a similar function. It does not automatically revert to its original form.
recalibration.accessory: The infection converts one of your own possessions into a different accessory, chosen by the GM. The replacement is of similar mass and size and serves a similar function. It does not automatically revert to its original form.

motivation.text: The next time, within the next 12 hours, you have the opportunity to enhance your own body, you have to use this opportunity, or try to fight your instinct to become something better.

revision.text: The GM defines a persistent physical alteration. It may be limiting, disturbing or ambiguously useful, and its severity and drama should scale to the situation the effect occurs in. The change cannot be revoked for the next 1 hour. After that, a workshop or healing vat with a matching morph blueprint removes it.

governor.limited: In Combat: The Morph can only use its lower listed movement rate. Out of Combat: The Morph moves and acts deliberately slow, as if trying to protect itself from wear and tear. Duration: 1d6 minutes.
governor.overridden: In Combat: The Morph must always use at least its higher listed movement rate whenever it moves. Out of Combat: The Morph moves deliberately fast and acts recklessly fast, as if trying to save time. Duration: 1d6 minutes.
governor.runaway: In Combat: The Morph must always move its maximum possible distance each action turn. Out of Combat: The Morph cannot stand still, as if stopping and going would be an imperfection leading to more wear, which must be prevented at all cost. Duration: 1d6 minutes.

compulsion.overdoIt: Gain the motivation Overdo It for 12 hours: you carry out every task with excessive thoroughness. You won't stop iterating on a task and trying to improve it, even if it is evidently finished. You may attempt a WIL Check to snap out of this compulsion.
compulsion.testTheLimits: Gain the motivation Test the Limits for 12 hours: you always push further than the situation requires. You are prone to even think of additional opportunities to enhance the task at hand, prompting people around you with ideas on how to proceed on an already finished task. You may attempt a WIL Check to snap out of this compulsion.
compulsion.redTape: Gain the motivation Red Tape for 12 hours: you act conspicuously slowly and cautiously, sometimes leaving work unfinished for fear of causing damage or breaking a safety limit. You may attempt a WIL Check to snap out of this compulsion.

calibration.efficiency: Once within the next 12 hours, after you declare an action, the GM may choose to run the morph in Efficiency mode: +10, but the task takes twice as long, or an opponent gains +10 in an opposed test.
calibration.experimental: Once within the next 12 hours, after you declare an action, the GM may choose to run the morph in Experimental mode: -10, but a successful effect is doubled where meaningful.
calibration.pushTheLimit: Once within the next 12 hours, after you declare an action, the GM may choose to push the morph past its limit: +10, and the morph takes DV 1d6 afterwards.

rerouting.boost: -30 to one skill in a pool category, chosen by the GM, buys +30 to one skill in a different category, also chosen by the GM. Duration: 1d6 minutes.
rerouting.support: -30 to one skill, chosen by the GM, buys +10 to all other skills in the same category. Duration: 1d6 minutes.
rerouting.switch: -10 to all skills in one category, chosen by the GM, buys +10 to all skills in another category, also chosen by the GM. Duration: 1d6 minutes.

pushing.overclocking: Once within the next 24 hours, after a test is rolled, the GM may raise its outcome by one degree - for example, turning a plain success into a superior success. The direction of the original result is never reversed. These effects tend to occur at the worst possible moment. They can never occur where doing so would put the Ki user's own physical or mental integrity at risk.
pushing.dampening: Once within the next 24 hours, after a test is rolled, the GM may lower its outcome by one degree - for example, turning a superior success into a plain success. The direction of the original result is never reversed. These effects tend to occur at the worst possible moment. They can never occur where doing so would put the Ki user's own physical or mental integrity at risk.
pushing.switching: Once within the next 24 hours the GM may flip-flop the two digits of a roll that has already come to rest - the same effect a pool point normally buys, for example turning a 71 into a 17 - except the GM applies it directly to this one roll instead of it costing you a pool point. These effects tend to occur at the worst possible moment. They can never occur where doing so would put the Ki user's own physical or mental integrity at risk.

carrier.location: For the next 1d6 minutes the morph cannot fall completely silent. It involuntarily broadcasts your exact location.
carrier.diagnostics: For the next 1d6 minutes the morph cannot fall completely silent. It involuntarily broadcasts its technical diagnostics.
carrier.sensorFeed: For the next 1d6 minutes the morph cannot fall completely silent. It involuntarily broadcasts excerpts from an active sensor feed.

saturation.text: Incoming signals bleed into your senses and interfaces without cause. Relevant Interface and Perceive tests suffer -20 for 1d6 minutes.

interference.whiteNoise: For 1d6 minutes the morph floods its surroundings with electromagnetic noise. Affected wireless links in the immediate area suffer -30, your own and your allies' included.
interference.signalBoost: For 1d6 minutes the morph amplifies the local electromagnetic environment instead. Every signal in the vicinity, your own included, becomes easier to detect and triangulate: +30 to locate them.

dependency.tacticalNetwork: For 12 hours you have to stay together with every member of your current group. If the signals separate too far, the network collapses and you suffer -20 to all actions until the group closes ranks again or the 12 hours run out.
dependency.ping: For 12 hours you have to perform a Ping - a Mesh scan - before you act in a new environment, whenever new people are present or the number of participants changes. Acting without it costs you -20 to all actions.
dependency.experimentalApi: For 12 hours you may not maintain any passive encryption. For as long as you do, you suffer -20 to all actions.

beacon.text: Once within the next 24 hours the GM may trigger an uncontrolled high-powered transmission. For 1d6 minutes the morph is easy to locate and cannot fall silent, and it quietly patches into existing connections nearby, without actually granting the affected user or the infection any real access. The transmission carries an unknown data pattern, such as coordinates, Exsurgent structures, or fragments of alien telemetry, but it does not transmit the infection.

fatigue.brittleArmor: The morph's Frame armor becomes brittle and flakes away: -4/-4 to its Frame armor for 1d6 minutes.
fatigue.fatiguedActuators: -30 to all SOM-based tests for 1d6 minutes.
fatigue.leakingConstruction: One existing environmental resistance ceases to function for 1d6 minutes.

seized.ware: Ware installed into the infected morph starts to misbehave - outages are common. One piece of ware, chosen by the GM, is completely blocked for 1d6 minutes.
seized.sense: Perception drops out mid-sentence, as if a channel had simply been unplugged. One sense, chosen by the GM, is completely blocked for 1d6 minutes.
seized.movement: Drive trains and actuators lock up mid-motion and refuse to answer. One movement mode, chosen by the GM, is completely blocked for 1d6 minutes.

intermittent.malfunction: Load-bearing subsystems answer more reluctantly every time they are pushed. For 12 hours the GM may call for a test whenever one specific piece of ware is used particularly hard. Which piece of ware is affected is decided by the GM the moment the effect first triggers.
intermittent.sensorDecay: The morph's sensor returns drift and smear until nothing reads cleanly. All Perceive tests suffer -20 for 1d6 hours.
intermittent.heuristicErrors: The morph's pattern matching decays and it misreads machines and people alike. Interface and Kinesics tests suffer -20 for 1d6 hours.

shedding.wareComponent: A piece of ware visibly decays and withers while staying attached to the morph. It cannot be repaired for 1d3 hours; once that time passes it recovers and works again on its own, but it still looks visibly broken until it receives an actual repair to hide the damage from view.
shedding.armorPlate: A plate of the morph's Frame armor visibly decays and flakes while staying attached, and provides no protection for as long as it stays in this brittle state. It cannot be repaired for 1d3 hours; once that time passes it recovers and works again on its own, but it still looks visibly broken until it receives an actual repair to hide the damage from view.

breakdown.text: Once in the next 24 hours the GM can trigger a systemic breakdown in a fitting moment. The breakdown can affect a maximum of two systems - a sense and a piece of ware, or two senses, and so on - and holds for 1d6 minutes before the body starts to recover. Depending on the situation this effect can still be visible afterwards if it is not properly repaired, but the Ki user fully recovers from the episode.

witnesses.eyes: Nearby sensor-equipped devices swing towards you at once: cameras, scanners, every lens in range. The effect works through walls and obstructions and fires even where nothing could actually see you. It is instantaneous and passes the moment attention has been drawn once. Anything that was not already in range - a few metres at most, at the GM's discretion - is not affected if it arrives afterwards. Whatever was recording can be used against you afterwards.
witnesses.attention: Nearby drones and synthmorphs turn towards you. Where a synth is piloted by an ego, that ego involuntarily looks in your direction; if you are hiding, you need a matching test to avoid being spotted, and the affected egos never know why they looked. The effect works through walls and obstructions and fires even where nothing could actually see you. It is instantaneous and passes the moment attention has been drawn once. Anything that was not already in range - a few metres at most, at the GM's discretion - is not affected if it arrives afterwards.

sympathetic.text: For 1d6 minutes the GM may set off nearby ware or objects whose function resembles whatever you are currently using, causing minor confusion and usually a -10 modifier. Lenses go blurry or unnaturally sharp, limbs move on their own, lights switch themselves on or off. Cyberbrains and life-support systems are excluded.

borrowed.eye: For 1d6 minutes the devices around you replace your own sight: instead of seeing normally, you see through the room's cameras. The GM may call for harder Perceive tests to reflect the unfamiliar viewpoint. The borrowed function is not recorded over the normal Mesh, but other means and other observers can still perceive it.
borrowed.hand: For 1d6 minutes the devices around you replace your own hands: instead of handling things yourself, you grip and move through the room's manipulators. The GM may call for harder tests for any fine manipulation. The borrowed function is not recorded over the normal Mesh, but other means and other observers can still perceive it.
borrowed.voice: For 1d6 minutes the devices around you replace your own voice: instead of speaking normally, you talk through the room's speakers. Anyone present to hear it may get a check to realize something is wrong. The borrowed function is not recorded over the normal Mesh, but other means and other observers can still perceive it.
borrowed.organ: For 1d6 minutes your morph keeps all of its own functions - instead, its state echoes out into the environment. Your thoughts surface in nearby chat windows, your vital signs are displayed as belonging to someone else, doors, pumps, ventilation or lighting pulse in your bodily rhythms. Anyone present to notice these effects may get a check to realize something is wrong. The echo is not recorded over the normal Mesh, but other means and other observers can still perceive it.

gathering.procession: For 1d6 minutes mobile and movable devices peel away from their tasks and trail after you in a ragged line. They do not deliberately attack, but they mark your path: anyone tracking you gains a bonus at the GM's discretion.
gathering.encirclement: For 1d6 minutes mobile and movable devices crowd in around you and block the way wherever you turn. They do not deliberately attack, but you move badly and keep stumbling over them for the full 1d6 minutes.
gathering.nest: For 1d6 minutes mobile and movable devices heap themselves onto you and work every reachable object into an improvised structure. They do not deliberately attack, but the pile blocks your sightlines: you count as distracted, -20 to everything, or at the very least suffer badly degraded visibility.

avatar.text: Once within the next 24 hours the GM may wake several local Mesh-connected devices as a single presence for 1d6 minutes, drawing on all or part of this list to build something that feels alien: speakers, displays and Mesh outputs communicating together; bots, manipulators and doors moving like parts of one organism; sensors, lights and radios forming a responsive perceptual network. The sensors involved do not feed into the affected devices' normal outputs, which show a Mesh interference signature for the duration instead. The GM controls the presence's behaviour, and you gain no command over it.
